runs.text: 1. Liquidity and maturities are the issuer's clearest strength. Cash of USD 172.7 million plus undrawn revolver capacity of USD 1,513.7 million gives USD 1,686.4 million, against current maturities of USD 195.1 million at September 30, 2026. The nearest bond maturity is USD 136.9 million of 7.500% notes due April 2027, then USD 550.0 million of 4.625% notes due December 2027. The revolver (USD 1,750.0 million commitment) and the term loan mature in November 2030 [CP-1 liquidity table and debt register]. 2. The debt stack is simple and mostly fixed-rate: six series of senior notes totalling USD 3,886.9 million, a USD 735.9 million term loan, a USD 235.0 million revolver draw, a USD 110.9 million headquarters facility, USD 160.5 million of finance leases and USD 76.1 million of mortgage and other debt. Total debt is USD 5,172.9 million at carrying value and USD 5,205.4 million before issuance costs. About 79% is fixed-rate. Security and guarantor terms for the notes are not supplied, so ranking cannot be assessed [CP-1 debt register; CP-0 gaps]. 3. Leverage is moderate-to-high on our estimate: 4.15x gross and 4.01x net on trailing EBITDA of USD 1,246.9 million built from printed operating income and depreciation and amortization, and interest cover of 4.87x on cash interest. The company reports a covenant leverage ratio of 3.69 against a maximum of 5.00 and targets 3.5x to 4.0x. No EBITDA appears in any source, so the covenant ratio cannot be rebuilt [CP-1 financials table]. 4. Operating results are mixed. Nine-month 2026 revenue rose 3.4% and operating income rose 3.7%, but the gross margin fell to 25.2% from 25.9%, funeral gross profit fell 5.5% on 2.7% fewer comparable services, and cemetery gross profit rose 5.3% [CP-1 calculation C12; CP-1A operating model]. On October 28, 2026 the issuer lowered its 2026 adjusted earnings per share outlook to USD 3.94 to 4.04 from USD 4.10 to 4.30 and kept its operating cash flow outlook midpoint at USD 1,085 million [CP-1A timeline]. 5. Cash generation is solid but is returned to shareholders. Operating cash flow less capital expenditure was USD 681.4 million for the last twelve months to Q3 2026 and USD 594.2 million in the nine months. Dividends and buybacks were USD 464.4 million in the nine months; in FY2025 they were USD 644.6 million, USD 90.3 million above operating cash flow less capital expenditure, while total debt rose USD 304.5 million [CP-1 calculations C3, CP-1A calculation C3]. 6. Visibility is supported by the backlog, which grew to USD 17.72 billion from USD 17.01 billion, but USD 9.15 billion is insurance-funded and not on the balance sheet, and future revenue exceeds trust assets, so cash received can lag revenue recognised [CP-1A operating model]. 7. Claims outside debt are modest relative to debt except trust and surety structures: operating leases (present value USD 50.8 million at December 31, 2025), unfunded retirement plans (USD 12.3 million), surety bonds of USD 498.3 million and unquantified unclaimed property audits in about forty states. Consolidated trust balances of USD 6,050.7 million and USD 2,448.4 million are matched by trust assets [CP-1 claims table]. 8. Two source conflicts are unresolved: the floating-rate average of 4.1% against 5.68% in the debt note, and the annual maturity table, whose caption and total do not agree. Interest sensitivity and the maturity ladder rest on the debt note and carrying values meanwhile [CP-1A conflicts].

runs.text: Strengths. Scale and diversification: the network of 1,491 funeral service locations and 506 cemeteries, with a cemetery segment protected by high barriers to entry, spreads local demand risk [Documentary Fact; CP-1A operating model]. Revenue visibility: the preneed backlog of USD 17.72 billion is recognised over time [Documentary Fact]. Liquidity and maturity profile: USD 1,686.4 million of liquidity and a bank facility maturing in November 2030 [Documentary Fact; CP-1]. Cash conversion: operating cash flow after capital expenditure of USD 681.4 million for the last twelve months to Q3 2026, equal to 13.2% of total debt [Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 C3 and C10]. Fixed-rate mix: about 79% of debt is fixed at a weighted average of 4.67%, which limits near-term interest cost swings [Documentary Fact; CP-1].

Weaknesses. Margin pressure: higher selling compensation, advertising and healthcare costs against falling funeral volumes in a high fixed-cost business, with a lowered 2026 outlook [Documentary Fact and Management Language; CP-1A]. Leverage that is moderate-to-high on our estimate at 4.15x gross, with a covenant definition that is not supplied and a management target of 3.5x to 4.0x [Analyst Interpretation; CP-1]. Distributions: dividends and buybacks absorb most free cash flow, so debt reduction is unlikely without a policy change [Analyst Interpretation; CP-1A governance]. Concentration: 32.2% of locations are in California, Texas and Florida, which the issuer itself flags as exposed to natural disasters [Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; CP-1A]. Preneed structure: surety bonds of USD 498.3 million and a USD 258.7 million trust-funding obligation if surety were not renewed at December 31, 2025 are contingent liquidity calls [Documentary Fact; CP-1A]. Missing creditor protections: the credit agreement restrictions, indentures, guarantor detail and ratings are not supplied [Insufficient Information].

runs.text: No acquisition of the issuer, sponsor investment, merger, spin-off or recapitalisation is described in the supplied sources, and the context lists no deal terms, quotes or ratings. The transaction row is therefore Insufficient Information, not an adverse conclusion. The financing events in the period under review are ordinary-course. In November 2025 the company amended its 2.2 billion US dollar credit agreement due January 2028 into a new 2.5 billion US dollar bank credit agreement due November 2030, made up of a 1.75 billion US dollar revolver (with a 100.0 million sublimit for letters of credit) and a 750.0 million US dollar term loan; at closing the term loan rose by a net 121.4 million and the revolver fell by a net 115.0 million (10-K page:102). The agreement is guaranteed by a majority of domestic subsidiaries and has a maximum leverage ratio and certain dividend and share repurchase restrictions. In September 2024 it issued 800.0 million US dollars of unsecured 5.750% Senior Notes due October 2032 (10-K page:102, page:123). A corporate headquarters debt facility due February 2037 funds the new headquarters; 110,852 thousand was drawn at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:18), and its commitment size and terms are Not supplied. In the nine months to September 30, 2026 the company issued or added 586.1 million US dollars of debt, all on the revolver (530.0 million) and the headquarters facility (56.1 million), and paid 570.7 million, including 550.0 million on the revolver (Q3 10-Q page:19); no senior notes were issued or redeemed. On June 11, 2026 the board raised the repurchase authorization by about 472.0 million US dollars, and 498.8 million remained at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:20). Subsequent to September 30, 2026 the company repurchased 232,968 shares for 18.2 million US dollars (Q3 10-Q page:20). The 7.500% Senior Notes due April 2027 are the nearest maturity and are within the current maturities of 195,060 thousand (CP-1). No new debt issue, refinancing or amendment dated after September 30, 2026 is in the sources.

fields.value: The reported financial base for SERVICE CORP INTERNATIONAL supports a stable consolidated credit view at September 30, 2026, with the leverage estimate and the covenant figure kept apart. Revenue for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was 3,307,004 thousand against 3,197,707 thousand a year earlier, operating income rose to 728,292 thousand from 702,537 thousand, and operating cash flow was 869,288 thousand against 729,860 thousand. Total debt printed on the balance sheet was 5,172,948 thousand against 5,139,817 thousand at December 31, 2025, and cash fell to 172,653 thousand from 243,581 thousand, so net debt rose while the company bought back 318,942 thousand of stock and paid 145,421 thousand of dividends. No EBITDA appears in any source, so all EBITDA ratios below are analyst estimates built from printed operating income and printed depreciation and amortization lines (C1); they are not the covenant measure, which the credit agreement defines and the sources do not. The company reports a covenant leverage ratio of 3.69 against a 5.00 maximum at September 30, 2026. The stack is mostly unsecured senior notes plus a bank term loan and revolver due November 2030, with the revolver largely undrawn, and the one near-term maturity is the 7.500% notes due April 2027. Open items are the maturity-table basis conflict, a floating-rate average that does not match the debt note, and the absence of the credit agreement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: SERVICE CORP INTERNATIONAL is the largest listed deathcare operator in North America by its own account, running 1,491 funeral service locations and 506 cemeteries at September 30, 2026, of which 317 combine both. It has no sponsor, no controlling holder disclosed in the sources and no pending or completed transaction in the period under review, so the credit question is operating durability and capital allocation rather than deal structure. The business model sells at the time of need and in advance. Advance sales build a deferred revenue backlog, 17.72 billion US dollars at September 30, 2026, whose revenue is recognised mainly at death or delivery, so cash and revenue are separated in time and part of the backlog (insurance-funded, 9.15 billion US dollars) is not on the balance sheet. Pricing power and cemetery growth currently offset lower funeral volumes. Management keeps a leverage target of 3.5x to 4.0x and returns cash through dividends and buybacks within covenant limits that are not supplied. For creditors the key facts are the scale and diversification of the network, the visibility of the backlog, the concentration in three states, the trust and surety structure that sits behind preneed sales, and a consistent pattern of returning cash to shareholders through dividends and buybacks. The main open items are ownership and board detail (proxy statement not supplied), the credit agreement payment restrictions, and the ratings that are not in the sources.

fields.value: No acquisition of the issuer, sponsor investment, merger, spin-off or recapitalisation is described in the supplied sources, and the context lists no deal terms, quotes or ratings. The transaction row is therefore Insufficient Information, not an adverse conclusion. The financing events in the period under review are ordinary-course. In November 2025 the company amended its 2.2 billion US dollar credit agreement due January 2028 into a new 2.5 billion US dollar bank credit agreement due November 2030, made up of a 1.75 billion US dollar revolver (with a 100.0 million sublimit for letters of credit) and a 750.0 million US dollar term loan; at closing the term loan rose by a net 121.4 million and the revolver fell by a net 115.0 million (10-K page:102). The agreement is guaranteed by a majority of domestic subsidiaries and has a maximum leverage ratio and certain dividend and share repurchase restrictions. In September 2024 it issued 800.0 million US dollars of unsecured 5.750% Senior Notes due October 2032 (10-K page:102, page:123). A corporate headquarters debt facility due February 2037 funds the new headquarters; 110,852 thousand was drawn at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:18), and its commitment size and terms are Not supplied. In the nine months to September 30, 2026 the company issued or added 586.1 million US dollars of debt, all on the revolver (530.0 million) and the headquarters facility (56.1 million), and paid 570.7 million, including 550.0 million on the revolver (Q3 10-Q page:19); no senior notes were issued or redeemed. On June 11, 2026 the board raised the repurchase authorization by about 472.0 million US dollars, and 498.8 million remained at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:20). Subsequent to September 30, 2026 the company repurchased 232,968 shares for 18.2 million US dollars (Q3 10-Q page:20). The 7.500% Senior Notes due April 2027 are the nearest maturity and are within the current maturities of 195,060 thousand (CP-1). No new debt issue, refinancing or amendment dated after September 30, 2026 is in the sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - **Revenue durability.** Evidence: backlog of 17.72 billion US dollars at September 30, 2026 and recognised preneed cemetery property revenue growth (Q3 10-Q page:31, page:40). Risk mechanic: revenue is recognised from earlier sales, which lowers volatility, but insurance-funded backlog is outside the balance sheet and future revenue exceeds trust assets (Q3 10-Q page:31). Credit implication: supports debt service visibility; the counter-evidence is falling funeral volume (nine-month services performed down 2.7%) and the lowered outlook, so the stability is revenue-side, not margin-side. No logged conflict counters this.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - **Margin and cash-flow risk.** Evidence: Q3 and nine-month gross margin fell while selling compensation, advertising and health insurance costs rose (Q3 10-Q page:38, page:40; CP-1 calculation C12). Risk mechanic: a high fixed-cost base and front-loaded selling costs on preneed growth cut near-term margin. Credit implication: coverage ratios could ease if volume keeps falling; the covenant ratio reported at 3.69 is below its 5.00 maximum, but its definition is Not supplied, and the conflict on floating-rate cost (below) limits interest-cost conclusions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - **Concentration risk.** Evidence: California, Texas and Florida are three of the largest states by revenue and hold 32.2% of locations (10-K page:25, page:11; C2). Risk mechanic: a single catastrophe or regulatory change in these states hits many locations at once. Credit implication: insurance and surety capacity matter; revenue by state is Not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - **Sponsor and capital allocation alignment.** Evidence: dividend payout target, buyback pace and leverage target (10-K page:18; Q3 10-Q page:20, page:25). Risk mechanic: returns to shareholders are discretionary and sized to cash flow; in FY2025 they exceeded operating cash flow less capex. Credit implication: creditors rely on management policy and covenant restrictions rather than a sponsor commitment; the restrictions are Not supplied, so legal capacity to increase distributions cannot be assessed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: SERVICE CORP INTERNATIONAL is a stable, cash-generative credit with moderate-to-high leverage that its liquidity comfortably supports. Its strongest support is a USD 17.72 billion preneed backlog, USD 1,686.4 million of liquidity at September 30, 2026 and a revolver and term loan that do not mature until November 2030. The weakest point is margin pressure: funeral volumes are falling, selling and healthcare costs are rising and the issuer lowered its 2026 earnings outlook, while distributions to shareholders stay high. Our estimated gross leverage of 4.15x is above the reported covenant ratio of 3.69x, and the covenant definition is not supplied. What decides the outcome is whether cemetery growth and pricing keep offsetting funeral volume loss without more debt-funded buybacks.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. Liquidity and maturities are the issuer's clearest strength. Cash of USD 172.7 million plus undrawn revolver capacity of USD 1,513.7 million gives USD 1,686.4 million, against current maturities of USD 195.1 million at September 30, 2026. The nearest bond maturity is USD 136.9 million of 7.500% notes due April 2027, then USD 550.0 million of 4.625% notes due December 2027. The revolver (USD 1,750.0 million commitment) and the term loan mature in November 2030 [CP-1 liquidity table and debt register].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. The debt stack is simple and mostly fixed-rate: six series of senior notes totalling USD 3,886.9 million, a USD 735.9 million term loan, a USD 235.0 million revolver draw, a USD 110.9 million headquarters facility, USD 160.5 million of finance leases and USD 76.1 million of mortgage and other debt. Total debt is USD 5,172.9 million at carrying value and USD 5,205.4 million before issuance costs. About 79% is fixed-rate. Security and guarantor terms for the notes are not supplied, so ranking cannot be assessed [CP-1 debt register; CP-0 gaps].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Leverage is moderate-to-high on our estimate: 4.15x gross and 4.01x net on trailing EBITDA of USD 1,246.9 million built from printed operating income and depreciation and amortization, and interest cover of 4.87x on cash interest. The company reports a covenant leverage ratio of 3.69 against a maximum of 5.00 and targets 3.5x to 4.0x. No EBITDA appears in any source, so the covenant ratio cannot be rebuilt [CP-1 financials table].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Operating results are mixed. Nine-month 2026 revenue rose 3.4% and operating income rose 3.7%, but the gross margin fell to 25.2% from 25.9%, funeral gross profit fell 5.5% on 2.7% fewer comparable services, and cemetery gross profit rose 5.3% [CP-1 calculation C12; CP-1A operating model]. On October 28, 2026 the issuer lowered its 2026 adjusted earnings per share outlook to USD 3.94 to 4.04 from USD 4.10 to 4.30 and kept its operating cash flow outlook midpoint at USD 1,085 million [CP-1A timeline].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. Cash generation is solid but is returned to shareholders. Operating cash flow less capital expenditure was USD 681.4 million for the last twelve months to Q3 2026 and USD 594.2 million in the nine months. Dividends and buybacks were USD 464.4 million in the nine months; in FY2025 they were USD 644.6 million, USD 90.3 million above operating cash flow less capital expenditure, while total debt rose USD 304.5 million [CP-1 calculations C3, CP-1A calculation C3].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 6. Visibility is supported by the backlog, which grew to USD 17.72 billion from USD 17.01 billion, but USD 9.15 billion is insurance-funded and not on the balance sheet, and future revenue exceeds trust assets, so cash received can lag revenue recognised [CP-1A operating model].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 7. Claims outside debt are modest relative to debt except trust and surety structures: operating leases (present value USD 50.8 million at December 31, 2025), unfunded retirement plans (USD 12.3 million), surety bonds of USD 498.3 million and unquantified unclaimed property audits in about forty states. Consolidated trust balances of USD 6,050.7 million and USD 2,448.4 million are matched by trust assets [CP-1 claims table].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 8. Two source conflicts are unresolved: the floating-rate average of 4.1% against 5.68% in the debt note, and the annual maturity table, whose caption and total do not agree. Interest sensitivity and the maturity ladder rest on the debt note and carrying values meanwhile [CP-1A conflicts].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Scale and diversification: the network of 1,491 funeral service locations and 506 cemeteries, with a cemetery segment protected by high barriers to entry, spreads local demand risk [Documentary Fact; CP-1A operating model]. Revenue visibility: the preneed backlog of USD 17.72 billion is recognised over time [Documentary Fact]. Liquidity and maturity profile: USD 1,686.4 million of liquidity and a bank facility maturing in November 2030 [Documentary Fact; CP-1]. Cash conversion: operating cash flow after capital expenditure of USD 681.4 million for the last twelve months to Q3 2026, equal to 13.2% of total debt [Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 C3 and C10]. Fixed-rate mix: about 79% of debt is fixed at a weighted average of 4.67%, which limits near-term interest cost swings [Documentary Fact; CP-1].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Margin pressure: higher selling compensation, advertising and healthcare costs against falling funeral volumes in a high fixed-cost business, with a lowered 2026 outlook [Documentary Fact and Management Language; CP-1A]. Leverage that is moderate-to-high on our estimate at 4.15x gross, with a covenant definition that is not supplied and a management target of 3.5x to 4.0x [Analyst Interpretation; CP-1]. Distributions: dividends and buybacks absorb most free cash flow, so debt reduction is unlikely without a policy change [Analyst Interpretation; CP-1A governance]. Concentration: 32.2% of locations are in California, Texas and Florida, which the issuer itself flags as exposed to natural disasters [Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; CP-1A]. Preneed structure: surety bonds of USD 498.3 million and a USD 258.7 million trust-funding obligation if surety were not renewed at December 31, 2025 are contingent liquidity calls [Documentary Fact; CP-1A]. Missing creditor protections: the credit agreement restrictions, indentures, guarantor detail and ratings are not supplied [Insufficient Information].
